strengths: The paper introduces an innovative benchmark paradigm, 'Causal Pathways', which structures complex GUI agent tasks into programmatically verifiable atomic steps. This effectively mitigates the reliability issues of current MLLM-based or final-state evaluations.
The proposed hierarchical framework, LightManus, provides a robust, cross-platform architecture that coordinates tasks across PC and Android platforms, outperforming existing baselines.
The construction and public release of a human-verified trajectory dataset of 523 sequences (with self-correcting pathways) is highly valuable for training future GUI agents.

The experimental evaluation is rigorous, showing the performance envelope of current frontier models (e.g., GPT-o3, Claude 3.5 Sonnet) and demonstrating the limits of localized trajectory fine-tuning (T-RFT) on smaller open-source models.
weaknesses: The absolute size of the benchmark (276 tasks) is somewhat modest compared to standard web agent datasets, which may limit the coverage of extreme edge cases.
The paper lacks comprehensive discussion in the main text regarding how the benchmark adapts to structural updates or layout shifts of the target applications/websites over time.

The core training details and formulation of Trajectory-Reinforced Fine-Tuning (T-RFT) are presented at a very high level, with critical implementation details deferred to the Appendix, making the methodology hard to fully evaluate from the main text alone.

strengths: Introduces a highly rigorous and reproducible benchmark design using the Causal Pathways (CPs) paradigm, which programmatically verifies intermediate atomic states and addresses the common issues of final-state-only evaluation in GUI agents.
Proposes a comprehensive set of well-formulated evaluation metrics (WPSR, MATCR, p-ATSR) that offer fine-grained insights into agent behavior, long-horizon coherence, and error attribution.
Constructs a high-quality, human-verified trajectory dataset (523 trajectories) containing diverse path choices and self-correcting sequences, which is a valuable resource for training robust agents.

Presents extensive experiments across various state-of-the-art closed and open-source MLLMs, showcasing the significant challenge of the benchmark and demonstrating the practical benefits of the proposed LightManus framework and T-RFT.
weaknesses: The description of the Trajectory-Reinforced Fine-Tuning (T-RFT) method in Section 4.4 is mostly conceptual. The technical and mathematical formulation comparing it to standard SFT and RL is lacking in the main body, making it hard to understand how the policy optimization principles are practically implemented.

The scale of the fine-tuning dataset is relatively small (278 trajectories used for training), which may limit the generalizability and explain why the performance of Qwen2.5-VL-7B-RFT plummets so severely on Level-2 and Level-3 tasks.

While the paper mentions decoupling abstract logic from physical execution, it is not fully clear how the benchmark handles potential environmental changes, API updates, or third-party app UI shifts over time, which is a common pain point for GUI agent evaluations.

strengths: The paper introduces 'Causal Pathways,' a novel and robust benchmark paradigm that addresses the critical reproducibility and evaluation challenges of GUI agents by organizing tasks into programmatically verifiable, atomic steps with deterministic outcomes.

A comprehensive and fine-grained evaluation framework is proposed, utilizing multi-level metrics (WPSR, MATCR, p-ATSR) and structured error attribution (KD, PE, OE) that provide deep diagnostic insights into agent failures.

The paper contributes a high-quality, human-verified dataset of 523 GUI operation trajectories that explicitly preserve behavioral diversity and self-correcting strategies, which is a valuable resource for the community.

The evaluation is thorough, benchmarking several state-of-the-art open-source and proprietary multimodal models (such as GPT-o3, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, and Gemini-2.5-Pro) in complex, cross-platform environments.
weaknesses: There is a lack of clarity regarding the dataset splits. Section 4.2 states that 523 trajectories were curated, but Section 5.1 states that the model was fine-tuned on only 278 trajectories. The paper does not clearly explain how the remaining trajectories were utilized or split for validation/testing.

The technical description of Trajectory-Reinforced Fine-Tuning (T-RFT) in Section 4.4 is mostly conceptual and lacks mathematical rigor. The exact loss function, reward formulation, and optimization details are not presented in the main text, making it difficult to distinguish T-RFT from standard Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT).

The novelty of the LightManus agent architecture is somewhat limited, as it primarily acts as a hierarchical workflow manager orchestrating existing low-level agent frameworks (Mobile-Agent-e and PC-Agent).

The size of the fine-tuning dataset (278 trajectories for training) is quite small, which likely explains the model's severe generalization bottleneck and high Structural Compliance Error (SCE) rates (47.9%) on Level-2 and Level-3 tasks.

strengths: The paper tackles a critical challenge in GUI agent research: the trade-off between ecological realism and verifiable deterministic evaluation (the 'Evaluation-Realism Dilemma').

The NaturalGAIA benchmark's design of separating logical causal pathways (derived from Wikidata) from narrative linguistic layers represents an elegant and scalable solution for generating long-horizon tasks.

The proposed LightManus-Jarvis framework introduces a practical 'macro-planning-micro-execution' architecture that demonstrates outstanding empirical improvements (e.g., raising WPSR from 21.1% to 45.6% under Claude-Sonnet-4.5) while significantly reducing token consumption (by 75%) and execution time (by 76%).
A rigorous, multi-level evaluation framework (WPSR, MATCR, p-ATSR) is developed, providing deep insights into agent failures (such as the persistent impact of Operational Errors).
weaknesses: While the task generation pipeline leverages Wikidata to automate causal skeleton construction, it still ultimately relies on a manual human-in-the-loop verification protocol, which introduces a bottleneck for scaling up the dataset size (currently containing 276 tasks).

The Jarvis execution kernel relies heavily on Android accessibility tree structure (XML structural perception) to bypass coordinate estimation errors. Its generalizability to platforms with sparse, missing, or deliberately obfuscated accessibility trees (e.g., custom web views, certain desktop environments) is not thoroughly explored.

Even with the proposed architecture, absolute success rates on Level-3 (Hard) tasks remain quite low (maxing out at 40% under Claude-Sonnet-4.5 and Gemini-3.0-Pro), highlighting that the reasoning-execution gap remains a significant open problem.

strengths: Proposes an elegant and rigorous methodology (NaturalGAIA) to generate complex, multi-app GUI tasks with deterministic ground truths by decoupling logical causal pathways on Wikidata from linguistic narratives.

Introduces highly informative, fine-grained hierarchical evaluation metrics (such as WPSR, MATCR, and p-ATSR) that allow researchers to analyze agent progress and attribute errors much more granularly than binary success metrics.

The proposed LightManus-Jarvis framework demonstrates a massive leap in performance, achieving a Weighted Pathway Success Rate of 45.6% (compared to 21.1% of the baseline) while dramatically slashing token consumption and duration by approximately 75%.
Thorough evaluation and validation, including generalization experiments on external benchmarks (AndroidWorld, Mind2Web) and a detailed qualitative error analysis.
weaknesses: Relying on the Android Accessibility tree for structural perception may fail in real-world scenarios where apps (like games, hybrid platforms, or custom-drawn interfaces) do not expose clean or complete accessibility nodes, which is not thoroughly discussed.

The dataset generation pipeline still heavily relies on a Human-in-the-Loop verification protocol, which bottlenecks the scalability and continuous updating of the benchmark to match live application updates.
Several figures (especially Figure 1, Figure 4, and Figure 10 in the appendix) are extremely dense, with small text that is difficult to read without significant zooming.

strengths: The conceptual framing of separating logical causal pathways from linguistic narratives to build GUI agent benchmarks is an interesting direction.
weaknesses: Severe Scientific Integrity and Validity Issues: The paper evaluates its framework on a wide array of non-existent and unreleased foundation models, including 'GPT-5.2', 'Claude-Sonnet-4.5', 'Gemini-3.0-pro', 'Gemini-3.0-flash', 'Qwen3-max', 'Qwen3-vl-plus', and 'Qwen3.5-397b-a17b'. The inclusion of these fictional models strongly suggests that the experimental results in Table 2 and throughout the paper are entirely fabricated or generated by an LLM simulating a future research paper.

Glaring Placeholders and Incomplete Content: The abstract contains an empty placeholder for the code link ('Our code is publicly available at:
 .'), making the benchmark and framework completely inaccessible.

Pervasive Writing and Editing Errors: The manuscript contains severe drafting errors that indicate lack of quality control. For example, in Section 1, the exact same clause is repeated in consecutive sentences: 'However, these fail to capture the cognitive non-linearity of human intent (Ye et al., 2025; ...). However, these fail to capture the cognitive non-linearity of human intent (Dong et al., 2025; ...).'

Grammatical and Formatting Flaws: The paper features several broken sentences and improper formatting, such as the sentence fragment in Section 3.1 ('As shown in the figure 2. To ensure scalability...') and 'As Table 1, our independent verifier...' in Section 5.1.
Lack of Reproducibility: Because the evaluated models do not exist and the code is not provided, none of the claims made in the paper can be verified or reproduced.
